dhp1:1: Thought is of all things first, thought is of all things foremost, of thought are all things made.
dhp1:3: If with thought corrupt a man speak or act,
dhp1:5: Suffering follows him, even as a wheel follows the hoof of the beast of burden.
dhp2:1: Thought is of all things first, thought is of all things foremost, of thought are all things made.
dhp2:3: If with thought of faith a man speak or act,
dhp2:5: Happiness follows him, even as a shadow never fading.
dhp3:1: “He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me;”
dhp3:3: If any cherish this thought, their hatred never ceases.
dhp4:1: “He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me;”
dhp4:3: If any cherish not this thought, their hatred ceases.
dhp5:1: For not by hatred are hatreds ever quenched here in this world.
dhp5:3: By love rather are they quenched. This is an eternal law.
dhp6:1: But others do not understand that we must here control ourselves;
dhp6:3: Yet let them understand this, and straight dissensions cease.
dhp7:1: Whoever lives looking for pleasure, exercising no restraint over his senses,
dhp7:3: Immoderate in his enjoyments, indolent, inert,
dhp7:5: Him Māra overpowers, even as the wind overpowers a tree of little strength.
dhp8:1: Whoever lives looking not for pleasure, exercising restraint over his senses,
dhp8:3: Moderate in his enjoyments, endowed with faith, exerting the power of his will,
dhp8:5: Him Māra does not overpower, even as the wind does not overpower a mountain of rock.
dhp9:1: Whoever, not free from impurity, lacking self-restraint and truth,
dhp9:3: Puts on the yellow robe, he is not worthy of the yellow robe.
dhp10:1: Whoever is free from impurity, firmly established in the moral precepts,
dhp10:3: Possessed of self-restraint and truth, he is worthy of the yellow robe.
dhp11:1: They who think to find the truth in falsehood, they who discern but falsehood in the truth,
dhp11:3: They never attain the goal of truth, but abide in the pasture-ground of error.
dhp12:1: They who have rightly discerned the true in its truth and the false in its falsity,
dhp12:3: They attain the goal of truth and abide in the pasture-ground of right thinking.
dhp13:1: Even as rain breaks through an ill-thatched house,
dhp13:3: So lust breaks through an ill-trained mind.
dhp14:1: Even as rain breaks not through a well-thatched house,
dhp14:3: So lust breaks not through a well-trained mind.
dhp15:1: Here he suffers; after death he suffers: the evildoer suffers in both places.
dhp15:3: He suffers, he is afflicted, seeing the impurity of his own past deeds.
dhp16:1: Here he rejoices; after death he rejoices: he that has done good works rejoices in both places.
dhp16:3: He rejoices, he rejoices exceedingly, seeing the purity of his own past deeds.
dhp17:1: Here he suffers, after death he suffers; the evildoer suffers in both places.
dhp17:3: He suffers to think, “I have done evil;” yet more does he suffer, gone to a place of suffering.
dhp18:1: Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices: he that has done good works rejoices in both places.
dhp18:3: He rejoices to think, “I have done good works;” yet more does he rejoice, gone to a world of bliss.
dhp19:1: Though he utter much that is sensible, if the heedless man be not a doer of the word,
dhp19:3: He is like a cowherd counting the cows of others, and has no part in the Religious Life.
dhp20:1: Though he utter little that is sensible, if a man live according to the Law,
dhp20:3: If he forsake lust and hatred and delusion, if he have right knowledge, if his heart is truly free,
dhp20:5: If he cling to naught in this world or in that which is to come, such a man has a share in the Religious Life.
